But in God's eyes, Omri lived an evil life—he was a new record-holder for being evil. He followed in the footsteps of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who not only sinned himself but dragged all of Israel into his sins, making God angry with their empty-headed, empty-hearted lives.
The rest of Omri's life, the impact he had, is all written in the official records of Israel's kings. Omri died and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became the next king.

Ahab, Omri's son, became king of Israel in the 38th year of Asa's reign in Judah. Ahab ruled over Israel for 22 years from Samaria. And this dude, Ahab, was even more openly evil before God than anyone before him—a new champion of evil! It wasn't enough for him to just copy the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. No, he took it to a whole new level. First, he married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Then he started serving and worshiping the god Baal. He built a temple for Baal in Samaria and even put an altar for Baal in it. And as if that wasn't bad enough, he also built a shrine for the goddess Asherah. He made the God of Israel angrier than all the kings of Israel before him combined.

It was during Ahab's rule that a guy named Hiel from Bethel rebuilt the city of Jericho, but it came at a crazy cost. As part of the ritual, he sacrificed his oldest son, Abiram, when they laid the foundation, and his youngest son, Segub, when they set up the gates. This was the exact fulfillment of what Joshua, son of Nun, had prophesied would happen.

title: Prophet's Drought Declaration & Raven Uber Eats?!
paragraphs: And then, out of nowhere, this dude Elijah the Tishbite, from among the settlers of Gilead, just walks up to King Ahab and says, “I swear on the living God of Israel, the one I serve, that for the next few years, it’s gonna be a total drought. Not a single drop of rain or even dew unless I give the word.”

Then God told Elijah, “Okay, you need to get out of here, like, right now. Head east and lay low at the Kerith Ravine, across the Jordan River. You can drink from the stream there, and don’t worry about food—I’ve already told the ravens to bring you meals.”
So Elijah did exactly what God said. He went and set up camp in the Kerith canyon. And for real, ravens brought him food for breakfast and dinner, and he drank from the stream.

After a while, the stream dried up because the drought was so bad. So God spoke to him again: “Alright, time to move. Get up and go to Zarephath in Sidon and stay there. I’ve arranged for a widow who lives there to feed you.”

So he got up and headed to Zarephath. When he got to the town entrance, he saw a widow gathering firewood. He called out to her, “Hey, could you please get me a little water in a jug? I’m super thirsty.” As she was going to get it, he added, “And while you’re at it, could you bring me a piece of bread or something?”

She replied, “I swear on your living God, I don’t even have a single piece of bread. All I have is a handful of flour in a jar and a little bit of oil in a bottle. You literally caught me gathering a few sticks to make one last meal for my son and me. After we eat it, we’re just going to die.”

Elijah told her, “Don’t even worry about it. Go ahead and do what you were planning. But first, make a small piece of bread for me and bring it here. Then you can go make a meal for you and your son with whatever is left. Because this is what the God of Israel says: ‘The flour jar won’t run out and the oil bottle won’t be empty until the day God sends rain and ends this drought.’”

And she just went and did it, exactly what Elijah asked. And it turned out just like he said—they had food to eat every single day. The flour jar never ran out and the oil bottle never became empty. It was God’s promise, delivered by Elijah, coming true down to the last letter.
Sometime later, the woman’s son got really sick. It got worse and worse, and then he just stopped breathing.
The woman said to Elijah, “Why did you even come here in the first place? You, a holy man, just had to show up, point out all my past mistakes, and get my son killed?”
Elijah just said, “Give me your son.”

He took the boy from her arms, carried him up to the room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed. Then he prayed, “Oh God, my God, why would you do something so terrible to this widow who’s been so good to me? Why would you take her son’s life?”

Three times, he stretched himself out on top of the boy, praying with everything he had, “God, my God, please bring this boy back to life!” And God heard Elijah’s prayer. He put breath back into the boy’s body—he was alive! Elijah picked him up, carried him downstairs, and gave him back to his mother. “Look,” Elijah said, “your son is alive!”
The woman said to Elijah, “Okay, now I get it. You’re for real a man of God. When you speak, it’s God speaking—it’s the real deal!”

title: Elijah vs. Team Baal: The Ultimate God-Off
paragraphs: A super long time went by. Then God's word came to Elijah. The drought was in its third year, which was wild. The message was: "Go show yourself to Ahab; I'm about to make it rain on the country." So Elijah went to go see Ahab. The drought in Samaria was no joke, like, it was severe.

Ahab called for Obadiah, the guy in charge of the palace. Obadiah was a real one, he truly feared God. Back when Jezebel was trying to wipe out all of God's prophets, Obadiah hid a hundred of them in two caves, fifty in each, and made sure they had food and water.

Ahab told Obadiah, "Go search the whole country, check every spring and stream. We gotta see if we can find enough grass to keep our horses and mules from literally dying." So they split up the country to search—Ahab went one way, and Obadiah went the other.
Obadiah was on his way when, boom, there was Elijah! Obadiah dropped to his knees, totally bowing down, and was like, "Is that really you, my master Elijah?"
"Yep," said Elijah, "it's me, for real. Now go tell your boss, 'Elijah's here.'"

Obadiah was shook. "What did I do to deserve this? Ahab's gonna kill me. I swear on your God, there isn't a single country my master hasn't sent people to find you. And if they said, 'He's not here,' he'd make them swear they couldn't find you. And now you're telling me to go tell him you've been found? The second I leave, God's Spirit will probably teleport you to who-knows-where. Then when I tell Ahab, you'll be gone, and he'll kill me. I've been serving God since I was a kid! Hasn't anyone told you what I did when Jezebel was hunting God's prophets? I risked my neck hiding a hundred of them—fifty to a cave—and made sure they got food and water. And now you want me to tell my master, 'Elijah's been found'? He'll kill me for sure!"
Elijah said, "As surely as the God of Angel Armies lives, the one I serve, I will 100% meet your master face-to-face today."
So Obadiah went straight to Ahab and told him. And Ahab went out to meet Elijah.
The second Ahab saw Elijah, he said, "So it's you, the guy who's been causing all this trouble in Israel!"

"It's not me who's been causing trouble," Elijah shot back, "it's you and your family. You've ghosted God's commands and started chasing after the local gods, the Baals. So here's the plan: Get everyone in Israel to Mount Carmel. And make sure you bring the special pets of Jezebel—the 450 prophets of the local gods, the Baals, and the 400 prophets of the goddess Asherah."
So Ahab got everyone in Israel, especially the prophets, to go to Mount Carmel.
Elijah stood up and called out the people: "How long are you gonna play both sides? If God is the real God, then follow him. If it's Baal, then follow him. Just pick one!"
No one said a thing. Crickets.

Then Elijah said, "I'm the only prophet of God left in Israel, and there are 450 prophets of Baal. So let's do this: they bring two bulls. They can pick one, cut it up, and put it on an altar with wood—but no fire. I'll do the same with the other bull. Then, you pray to your god, and I'll pray to my God. The god who answers with fire? That's the real God."
Everyone was like, "Good plan, let's do it!"
Elijah told the Baal prophets, "You guys go first, there are more of you. Pick your bull, get it ready, and pray to your god, but don't light the fire."

So they took the bull, prepped it, and prayed to Baal all morning, shouting, "O Baal, answer us!" But nothing. Not even a whisper. They got so desperate they were jumping and dancing all over the altar they made.

By noon, Elijah started trolling them. "Maybe you should shout louder! He's a god, right? Maybe he's meditating, or busy with a project, or on vacation. You don't think he overslept and needs a wake-up call, do you?" So they yelled even louder and started cutting themselves with swords and knives, which was their ritual, until they were covered in blood.
This went on all afternoon. They tried every religious trick in the book to get something to happen, but still nothing. Not a sound, not a flicker.

Then Elijah told the people, "Okay, that's enough. My turn. Everyone, come here." So they all gathered around. He rebuilt God's altar, which was a wreck. He took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes of Jacob (the same Jacob God renamed Israel). He built the altar in God's name and then dug a big trench around it. He put the wood on the altar, cut up the bull, put it on the wood, and said, "Fill four big jars with water and pour it all over the bull and the wood." Then he said, "Do it again," and they did. "Do it a third time," and they did. The whole altar was soaked, and the trench was full of water.

When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet went up and prayed, "O God, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show them right now that you are God in Israel and that I'm your servant, doing all this because you told me to. Answer me, God, answer me and show these people that you are the one true God, and that you're giving them another chance to come back to you."
Instantly, fire from God fell from the sky and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, the dirt, and even all the water in the trench.
When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and started worshiping, yelling, "God is the true God! God is the true God!"
Elijah commanded them, "Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let a single one get away!"
They grabbed them all. Elijah took them down to the Kishon Brook and had them all executed.
Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go on, get up, eat and drink. Celebrate! Rain is coming. I can hear it."
Ahab went and ate and drank. Meanwhile, Elijah climbed to the top of Mount Carmel, bowed down low in prayer with his face between his knees. Then he told his servant, "Go look toward the sea."
He went, looked, and came back, "I don't see anything."
"Keep looking," Elijah said, "seven times if you have to."
And on the seventh time, the servant said, "Oh, wait, I see a cloud! But it's tiny, like the size of a hand, coming up from the sea."
"Quick!" Elijah said. "Go tell Ahab, 'Get in your chariot and get down the mountain before the rain traps you.'"

And then everything happened super fast. The sky turned black with clouds and wind, and then a massive downpour started. Ahab was racing his chariot back to Jezreel. And God gave Elijah a huge boost of strength. He tucked his robe into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.

title: Elijah's Burnout & God's Whisper
paragraphs: So Ahab went and told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, including how he totally wrecked her prophets. Jezebel was livid and sent a messenger to Elijah with a threat: “The gods are gonna get you for this, and I'm gonna get you. By this time tomorrow, you'll be just as dead as every one of those prophets.”

When Elijah heard this, he freaked out and ran for his life to Beersheba, way down in the south of Judah. He left his young assistant there and then walked for a whole day into the desert. He found a random broom bush, collapsed in its shade, and was just so done with everything. He wanted to die. “I’ve had enough, God! Just take my life—I’m ready to join my ancestors.” Totally exhausted, he fell asleep right there under the bush.
Suddenly, an angel shook him awake and said, “Get up and eat!”
He looked around and, what do you know, right by his head was a loaf of bread baked on some coals and a jug of water. He ate and drank, then went back to sleep.
The angel of God came back, shook him awake again, and said, “Get up and eat some more—you’ve got a long trip ahead of you.”

So he got up, ate and drank until he was full, and then started walking. That one meal gave him enough energy to walk for forty days and forty nights, all the way to Horeb, the mountain of God. When he got there, he crawled into a cave and fell asleep.
Then the word of God came to him: “So, Elijah, what are you doing here?”

“I’ve been going all out for the God-of-the-Angel-Armies,” Elijah said. “The people of Israel have ditched your covenant, wrecked the places of worship, and murdered your prophets. I’m the only one left, and now they’re trying to kill me too.”
Then he was told, “Go, stand at attention on the mountain before God. God is about to pass by.”

A crazy hurricane-level wind ripped through the mountains and shattered rocks in front of God, but God wasn't in the wind. After the wind, there was an earthquake, but God wasn't in the earthquake. And after the earthquake, there was a fire, but God wasn't in the fire. And after the fire, there was a gentle, quiet whisper.

When Elijah heard that quiet voice, he pulled his cloak over his face, went to the entrance of the cave, and just stood there. A quiet voice asked, “So Elijah, for real, what are you doing here?” Elijah repeated himself, “I’ve been working my heart out for God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, because the people of Israel have abandoned your covenant, destroyed your places of worship, and murdered your prophets. I’m the only one left, and now they’re trying to kill me.”

God said, “Go back the way you came, through the desert to Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as the new king of Aram. Then anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king of Israel. And finally, anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel Meholah to take over for you as prophet. Anyone who escapes from Hazael will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes from Jehu will be killed by Elisha. But listen, I’m keeping seven thousand people for myself—all the knees that haven’t bowed down to the god Baal and all the mouths that haven’t kissed his idol.”

Elijah left right away and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was out in a field plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and Elisha was with the twelfth team. Elijah went up to him and threw his cloak over him.
Elisha just left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Please! Let me just kiss my mom and dad goodbye—then I’ll follow you.”
“Go ahead,” said Elijah, “but don't forget what I just did to you.”

So Elisha went back, took his team of oxen, and butchered them. He used the plowing equipment to make a fire and cooked the meat—a real farewell feast for his family. Then he left and followed Elijah, becoming his right-hand man.

title: My Enemy is My Brother?? King Ahab's Big Mistake
paragraphs: So, around this time, King Ben-Hadad of Aram got his army together. He also roped in 32 local chiefs with their horses and chariots. They rolled up to Samaria and surrounded it, ready for war. He sent a messenger to King Ahab of Israel with a message: 'Yo, Ben-Hadad says your silver, gold, and the best of your wives and kids are his now.'
The king of Israel was like, 'Okay, whatever you say, my lord; I and everything I have is yours.'

But then the messenger came back a second time and was like, 'Actually, on second thought, I want *everything*. Your silver, your gold, all your wives, all your kids. Hand it all over. You've got 24 hours. Then my guys are coming to search your palace and your officials' houses and take whatever they think is cool.'

King Ahab called all his elders and was like, 'Can you believe this guy? He's just trying to start something. He wants to completely clean me out, demanding all my wives and children, even after I already agreed to pay him a ton!'
The elders and the people were all, 'Don't do it! Don't give him anything.'
So he told Ben-Hadad's messenger, 'Tell my lord, I was fine with the first deal, but this new one? I can't. I won't do it.'
The messenger went back and delivered the answer.
Ben-Hadad shot back his response: 'I swear to the gods, there won't be anything left of Samaria but dust by the time I'm done.'
King Ahab shot back, 'You know, it's a lot easier to talk tough than to actually win a fight.'
It turned out, when Ben-Hadad heard this comeback, he was already day-drinking with his chiefs in their tents. Super drunk, he just yelled, 'Get 'em!' and they attacked the city.
Just then, a random prophet shows up to King Ahab and says, 'God's message: See this huge army? Well, guess what? I'm handing them over to you today. And you'll know for sure that I am God.'
Ahab was like, 'For real? And who's gonna make this happen?'
God said, 'The young soldiers of the regional chiefs.'
'And who,' asked Ahab, 'gets to strike the first blow?'
God said, 'You do.'
Ahab checked out the young soldiers of the regional chiefs; he counted 232 of them. Then he checked his whole army—7,000 troops.
At noon they marched out after Ben-Hadad who, with his 32 allied chiefs, was busy getting wasted in their tents. The young soldiers led the charge.
A report came to Ben-Hadad: 'Uh, there are guys coming from Samaria.'
He said, 'If they're coming in peace, take them hostage. If they're coming to fight, do the same thing—take them hostage.'

The young soldiers poured out of the city with the whole army right behind them. They went hard in hand-to-hand combat. The Arameans bailed, with Israel right on their tail. But King Ben-Hadad of Aram escaped on a horse with his cavalry.
The king of Israel wrecked their horses and chariots—it was a huge loss for Aram.

A bit later, the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, 'Stay sharp—build up your army, figure out what you're capable of, and see what needs to be done. Before the year is over, the king of Aram will be back and he'll be strong.'

Meanwhile, the advisors to the king of Aram said, 'Their god is a god of the mountains—we have no chance against them there. So let's fight them on the flat plains where we'll have the upper hand. Here's the plan: replace every chief with a pro officer. Then get an army the same size as the one that bailed—horse for horse, chariot for chariot. And we'll fight them on the plains—we're sure to be stronger than them.'
The king thought it sounded like a good plan, so he did it.

When the new year came, Ben-Hadad gathered his army and they went up to Aphek to fight Israel. The Israelite army got ready and went to meet them. They set up in two camps, looking like two small flocks of goats. The whole plain was crawling with Arameans.

Just then a holy man came to the king of Israel and said, 'This is God's word: Because Aram said, "God is a god of the mountains and not a god of the valleys," I'll hand over this massive army to you. Then you'll know that I am God.'

The two armies just stared each other down for seven days. On the seventh day, the fight broke out. The Israelites took out 100,000 of the Aramean foot soldiers in one day. The rest of the army ran for their lives back to the city, Aphek, but then the city wall fell on 27,000 of the survivors.

Ben-Hadad escaped into the city and hid in a closet. Then his advisors told him, 'Look, we've heard the kings of Israel are pretty fair. Let's wear old rags, carry a white flag, and go to the king of Israel. Maybe he'll let you live.'
So that's what they did. They dressed in old rags, carried a white flag, and came to the king of Israel saying, 'Your servant Ben-Hadad said, "Please let me live."'
Ahab said, 'You're telling me he's still alive? If he's alive, he's my brother.'
The men saw this as a good sign and figured everything would be okay: 'Ben-Hadad is definitely your brother!'
The king said, 'Go get him.' They went and brought him back in a chariot.

Ahab said, 'I'm willing to give back the cities my father took from your father. And you can set up your own trade base in Damascus just like my father did in Samaria. I'll send you home safely.' Then he made a treaty with him and let him go.
A man who was one of the prophets said to a random guy, 'Hit me; hurt me. Do it for God—it's his command. Hit me; hurt me.' But the guy wouldn't do it.
So he told him, 'Because you didn't obey God's orders, a lion is going to attack you as soon as you leave.' And no sooner had the man left, a lion met him and attacked.
He then found another man and said, 'Hit me; hurt me.' That man did it—hit him hard in the face, and he started bleeding.

Then the prophet went and waited on the road for the king, with a bandage over his eyes to disguise himself. It wasn't long before the king came by. The man yelled out to the king, 'Your servant was in the middle of the battle when a guy showed up and gave me a prisoner, saying, "Guard this man with your life; if he goes missing you'll pay big time." But I got busy with other stuff and the next thing I knew, he was gone.'
The king of Israel said, 'You just decided your own punishment.'
At that, the man tore the bandage off his eyes and the king recognized who he was—one of the prophets!
The man said to the king, 'God's word: Because you let a man go who God had sentenced to die, it's now your life for his, and your people for his.'
The king of Israel went home super annoyed. He got back to Samaria in a really bad mood.

title: The King Who Got CANCELLED for Stealing a Vineyard
paragraphs: So, get this. On top of everything else, this happened: Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel right next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria. One day, Ahab hits up Naboth and says, “Yo, let me get that vineyard. I wanna turn it into a vegetable garden since it’s right next to my house—super convenient. I’ll trade you for a way better vineyard, or if you want, I’ll just pay you cash for it.”

But Naboth was like, “Not a chance. I swear to God, I would never sell you my family’s land.” Ahab went home in a total mood, sulking over what Naboth the Jezreelite said: “I’ll never hand over my family’s inheritance to you.” He went to bed, shoved his face in his pillow, and refused to eat.
His wife Jezebel came to him and was like, “What’s going on? Why are you so salty and refusing to eat?”

He told her, “Because I talked to Naboth the Jezreelite. I said, ‘Give me your vineyard—I’ll pay you for it or, if you’d rather, I’ll give you another vineyard in exchange.’ And he said, ‘I’ll never give you my vineyard.’”

Jezebel was like, “Is this seriously how a king of Israel acts? Aren't you the one in charge? Get up! Eat something! Cheer up! I’ll handle this. I’ll get you that vineyard from Naboth the Jezreelite.”

She wrote letters using Ahab’s name, stamped them with his official seal, and sent them to the elders and leaders in Naboth’s city. She wrote, “Announce a fast day and give Naboth the seat of honor. Then get a couple of phonies to sit across from him and publicly accuse him, saying, ‘You! You cursed God and the king!’ Then they’ll drag him out and stone him to death.”

And they actually did it. The men of the city—the elders and leaders—followed the instructions Jezebel wrote in the letters. They called for a fast day and sat Naboth at the head table. Then they brought in two liars and sat them across from Naboth. In front of everyone, the two degenerates accused him, “He cursed God and the king!” So the crowd dragged him out into the street, stoned him without mercy, and he died.

When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she told Ahab, “Go for it, Ahab—take Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard for yourself, the one he refused to sell you. Naboth is gone. Naboth is dead.”
The second Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite and claimed it as his own.

Then God stepped in and spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, “Get up, go down and confront Ahab, king of Israel, in Samaria. You’ll find him in Naboth’s vineyard; he’s gone there to claim it. Say this to him: ‘This is God’s word: What’s going on here? First murder, then theft?’ Then tell him, ‘This is God’s verdict: In the exact spot where the dogs licked up Naboth’s blood, they’ll lick up your blood—that’s right, your blood.’”
Ahab shot back at Elijah, “My enemy! So, you’ve found me.”

“Yeah, I’ve found you out,” said Elijah. “And because you’ve sold yourself out to do evil, defying God, ‘I’m definitely bringing disaster on you, I’ll destroy your descendants, and I’ll get rid of every single guy even remotely connected to your family. I’ll bring the same fate on you that happened to Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah—you’ve made me that angry by leading Israel into sin.’”

And about Jezebel, God said, “Dogs will fight over Jezebel’s body all over Jezreel. Any of Ahab’s family who dies in the city will be eaten by stray dogs; and if they die in the country, they’ll be eaten by vultures.”

Ahab, egged on by his wife Jezebel and in total defiance of God, set a new record for making a business out of evil. He got into some seriously messed up stuff with idols, just like the Amorites who God had kicked out of Israelite territory before.

When Ahab heard what Elijah said, he tore his clothes, put on rough burlap to show he was sorry, and fasted. He even slept in coarse burlap pajamas. He started walking around super quietly, like a mouse.
Then God spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: “Do you see how sorry Ahab is acting? Because he’s repenting, I won’t bring the disaster while he’s alive; but his son will get it.”

title: King Goes Undercover & It Ends BADLY
paragraphs: So for three years, everything was chill—no beef between Aram and Israel. Then, in the third year, King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to meet up with the king of Israel. The king of Israel said to his crew, "Yo, do you guys realize Ramoth Gilead is actually ours, and we're just sitting here doing nothing instead of taking it back from the king of Aram?"
He turned to Jehoshaphat and was like, "You down to roll with me and fight for Ramoth Gilead?"
Jehoshaphat said, "For sure. I'm with you 100%—my squad is your squad, my horses are your horses." Then he added, "But hold up, before we do anything, let's ask God for some guidance."
So the king of Israel got all his prophets together—all 400 of them—and asked, "Should I go attack Ramoth Gilead? Or should I chill?"
They all shouted, "Go for it! God will totally hand it over to you."
But Jehoshaphat was hesitant. "Is there maybe another prophet of God around here we can check with?"
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "Well, there is one more guy, Micaiah son of Imlah. But honestly, I hate him. He never says anything good about me, only bad news, doom and gloom."
"Bro, a king shouldn't talk like that about a prophet," said Jehoshaphat.
So the king of Israel told one of his guys, "Go get Micaiah son of Imlah, and be quick about it."

Meanwhile, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat were sitting on their thrones, decked out in their royal robes, right in front of the Samaria city gates. All the prophets were putting on a big show for them. This one dude, Zedekiah son of Kenaanah, even made some iron horns and was waving them around yelling, "God's word! With these, you're gonna wreck Aram until they're completely gone!" And all the other prophets were hyping him up, like, "Yeah! Go attack Ramoth Gilead! It's an easy win! God's giving it to you!"
The messenger who went to get Micaiah told him, "Listen, all the other prophets are saying the king will win. You should just agree with them and say yes too."
But Micaiah was like, "As God is my witness, I'm only gonna say what God tells me to say."
When Micaiah showed up, the king asked him, "So, Micaiah—should we attack Ramoth Gilead, or nah?"
He replied sarcastically, "Oh yeah, go for it. It'll be an easy win. God's gift to the king."
The king shot back, "Cut it out. How many times do I have to make you swear you'll only tell me the truth from God?"

"Alright, fine," Micaiah said, "since you're insisting. I had a vision of all of Israel scattered across the hills, like sheep without a shepherd. And God said, 'These poor people have no leader. Let them just go home and try to survive.'"
The king of Israel turned to Jehoshaphat and said, "See! What did I tell you? He never has anything good to say about me from God, only doom."

Micaiah wasn't finished. "I'm not done yet; listen to God's word: I saw God on his throne, and the entire angel armies of heaven were standing at attention on his right and his left. And God asked, 'Who can trick Ahab into attacking Ramoth Gilead so he'll die?' They all had different ideas. Then one spirit stepped up and said, 'I'll do it.' 'How?' God asked. 'Easy,' the spirit said, 'I'll go and make all his prophets lie.' And God said, 'That'll work. Go on, trick him.'"
"So that's what's happening right now. God has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all your puppet prophets. God has declared your doom."
Just then, Zedekiah son of Kenaanah walked up and punched Micaiah in the face, saying, "Oh really? Since when did the Spirit of God leave me to go talk to you?"
Micaiah shot back, "You'll find out soon enough, when you're desperately looking for a place to hide and can't find one."

The king of Israel was furious. "Get Micaiah out of here! Hand him over to Amon the city magistrate and to Joash the king's son with this message: 'King's orders: Throw him in jail and only give him bread and water until I get back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you actually get back safely, then I'm not a real prophet of God."
He then yelled to the crowd, "When it all goes down, people, remember you heard it here first!"

So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to attack Ramoth Gilead. The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "You wear my royal robes; I'm gonna go into battle in disguise." So the king of Israel went into the fight undercover.
Meanwhile, the king of Aram had given his 32 chariot commanders one order: "Don't waste your time with anyone else, big or small; go after the king of Israel and only him."

When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat in the king's robes, they thought, "There he is! The king of Israel!" and they went straight for him. Jehoshaphat screamed, and the commanders realized they had the wrong guy—it wasn't the king of Israel. So they left him alone.

But then, some random soldier just shot an arrow into the air without aiming, and it hit the king of Israel right in a gap in his armor. The king told his chariot driver, "Turn around! Get me out of here—I'm hit."

The battle raged all day. The king, propped up in his chariot, had to watch from the sidelines. He died that evening, and his blood pooled in the chariot. As the sun set, a shout went through the army: "Everyone go home! The king is dead!"

They brought the king's body to Samaria and buried him there. They washed his chariot at the pool of Samaria, where the town prostitutes bathed, and dogs licked up his blood, just like God had said would happen.

The rest of Ahab's story—everything he did, the fancy ivory palace he built, the towns he founded, and the defense system he built up—it's all written down in the official records of the kings of Israel. He was buried with his ancestors, and his son Ahaziah became the next king.

Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab's reign in Israel. Jehoshaphat was 35 when he started his 25-year rule in Jerusalem. His mom was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. He basically followed in his dad Asa's footsteps—no detours, no dead ends—living a life that pleased God. But he messed up by not getting rid of the local shrines where people worshiped other gods. And he stayed on good terms with the king of Israel.

The rest of Jehoshaphat's life, his accomplishments and his wars, are all in the official records of the kings of Judah. He also got rid of the male shrine prostitutes that were still around from his father Asa's time.
During his reign, Edom didn't have a king; a governor was in charge.

Jehoshaphat built some big ships to go get gold from Ophir. But they never even made it out of the harbor; they wrecked at Ezion Geber. Around that time, Ahaziah, Ahab's son, suggested they team up on a shipping business, but Jehoshaphat turned him down.
Then Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoram became the next king.

Ahaziah, son of Ahab, became king of Israel in Samaria during the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah. He was king for two years. And in God's eyes, he was a total failure, just living the same evil life as his parents and repeating the sinful patterns set by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who first led Israel into sin. By worshiping Baal, he made God, the God of Israel, super angry. If anything, he was even worse than his dad.
